svg.title: Marquee: Flash-Sale Ticketing
svg.desc:
Marquee: Flash-Sale Ticketing. Marquee (a made-up company) sells 60,000 stadium seats to 1.8 million fans who all arrive at 10:00. A virtual waiting room at the edge admits fans at a rate the origin can handle. Seat Inventory holds seats for 8 minutes while the fan pays, the Payment Orchestrator fails over between two card processors, and a transactional outbox streams every order to Kafka, where ticketing and the promoter's live dashboard read it at their own pace. It has 3 pages: On-Sale (Live), Regions & Failover and Start Here: A 5-Minute Tour. Together they hold 36 components.
Page On-Sale (Live) holds 27 components in 5 swimlanes, joined by 34 wires.
Page On-Sale (Live): Swimlanes - Fans (Phones and browsers): Fans and Marquee App. - Edge (Close to the fan): Realtime Hub, Edge CDN + WAF, Virtual Waiting Room and Legacy SMS Gateway. - Platform (Shared services): Bot & Fraud Check, Identity, Load Balancer, API Gateway, Ticket Wallet, Notifications and Push & Email. - On-Sale Core (Seats, orders, tickets): Seat Map Cache, Ticket Database, Seat Inventory, Checkout & Orders, Hold Expiry Sweeper, Ticket Jobs and Ticket Issuer. - Payments & Events (Money, Kafka, insight): Payment Orchestrator, Card Processor A, Card Processor B, Pay in 3, Order Events, Ticket Dead Letters and Promoter Dashboard.
Page On-Sale (Live): Frames - Frame PCI DSS scope holds Payment Orchestrator. - Frame After payment: tickets & messages (async) holds Ticket Jobs, Ticket Issuer, Notifications and Push & Email.
Page On-Sale (Live): Main flows - Fans calls Marquee App for “Tap "Buy" at 10:00”. - Marquee App calls Edge CDN + WAF over GraphQL for “HTTPS” (about 25 ms). - Realtime Hub exchanges data with Marquee App over Custom for “Live seat map”. - Edge CDN + WAF calls Virtual Waiting Room over HTTP for “No token” (about 2 ms), Load Balancer over HTTP for “Token valid: skip the line” (about 2 ms) and Ticket Wallet over HTTP for “Get ticket” (about 30 ms). - Virtual Waiting Room calls Load Balancer over HTTP for “Admitted” (about 1 ms). - Load Balancer calls API Gateway over HTTP for “Route” (about 1 ms). - API Gateway calls Identity over gRPC for “Verify session” (about 4 ms), Bot & Fraud Check over gRPC for “Bot score” (about 9 ms), Seat Map Cache over gRPC for “Read seat map” (about 2 ms), Seat Inventory over gRPC for “Hold” (about 5 ms) and Checkout & Orders over gRPC for “Checkout” (about 6 ms). - Seat Map Cache calls Ticket Database over SQL for “Miss: load” (about 6 ms). - Ticket Database sends messages to Order Events over Kafka for “CDC: OrderConfirmed”. - Seat Inventory calls Ticket Database over SQL for “Lock rows” (about 9 ms) and sends messages to Realtime Hub over AMQP for “Seat taken / freed”. - Checkout & Orders calls Seat Inventory over gRPC for “Sold” (about 5 ms), Ticket Database over SQL for “Order + outbox” (about 8 ms) and Payment Orchestrator over gRPC for “Authorise” (about 12 ms). - Hold Expiry Sweeper calls Seat Inventory over gRPC for “Release expired holds” (about 5 ms). - Payment Orchestrator calls Card Processor A over HTTP for “Card auth” (about 350 ms), Card Processor B over HTTP for “Fail over” (about 410 ms) and Pay in 3 over HTTP for “Instalments (planned)”. - Order Events sends messages to Ticket Jobs over Kafka for “Issue tickets” and Promoter Dashboard over Kafka for “Sales per second”. - Ticket Jobs sends messages to Ticket Dead Letters over AMQP for “5 tries” and Ticket Issuer over AMQP for “Issue”. - Ticket Dead Letters sends messages to Ticket Jobs over AMQP for “Redrive after fix”. - Ticket Issuer calls Ticket Wallet for “Write PDF + pass” (about 40 ms) and sends messages to Notifications over AMQP for “Issued”. - Notifications calls Push & Email over HTTP for “Push + email” (about 60 ms) and Legacy SMS Gateway over HTTP for “SMS, no app” (about 90 ms). - Push & Email sends messages to Marquee App over HTTP for “Tickets ready”.
Page On-Sale (Live): Queues - Order Events is a queue between Ticket Database and Ticket Jobs and Promoter Dashboard. It keeps messages for 7 days. - Ticket Jobs is a FIFO queue between Order Events and Ticket Dead Letters and Ticket Issuer. It holds up to 5000 messages and sends overflow to Ticket Dead Letters. It keeps messages for 4 days. - Ticket Dead Letters is a queue between Ticket Jobs and Ticket Jobs. It keeps messages for 14 days.
Page On-Sale (Live): Load balancers - Load Balancer is a load balancer for Edge CDN + WAF and Virtual Waiting Room. It spreads traffic over API Gateway, least connections.
Page On-Sale (Live): Caches, limiters and schedulers - Virtual Waiting Room is a rate limiter that admits 2 of every 5 requests to Load Balancer. - Seat Map Cache is a cache that answers 92% of reads, backed by Ticket Database. - Hold Expiry Sweeper is a scheduler (30s) that starts Seat Inventory. - Card Processor A is run by someone else. - Card Processor B is run by someone else. - Pay in 3 is run by someone else. - Order Events is a stream: Ticket Jobs and Promoter Dashboard each get every message. - Push & Email is run by someone else.
Page On-Sale (Live): Levels - Seat Inventory opens into 4 components in 3 swimlanes. - Payment Orchestrator opens into 6 components in 2 swimlanes.
Page Regions & Failover holds 9 components in 3 swimlanes, joined by 9 wires.
Page Regions & Failover: Swimlanes - Global (DNS and traffic steering): Fans and Global Traffic Manager. - eu-west (active) (Serves every fan today): eu-west stack, Ticket DB (eu), Nightly Snapshots and Backup Job. - us-east (warm standby) (Takes over in under 5 min): us-east stack, Ticket DB (us) and Backup Vault.
Page Regions & Failover: Frames - Frame Disaster recovery: RPO 1 s, RTO 5 min holds nothing.
Page Regions & Failover: Main flows - Fans calls Global Traffic Manager for “DNS lookup” (about 20 ms). - Global Traffic Manager calls eu-west stack over HTTP for “100% today” (about 30 ms) and us-east stack over HTTP for “0%, until failover” (about 90 ms). - eu-west stack calls Ticket DB (eu) over SQL for “Read / write”. - us-east stack calls Ticket DB (us) over SQL for “Read (standby)”. - Ticket DB (eu) sends messages to Ticket DB (us) over SQL for “Async replication”. - Nightly Snapshots calls Backup Job for “Start job”. - Backup Job calls Backup Vault for “Upload + read back” and Ticket DB (eu) over SQL for “Read snapshot”.
Page Regions & Failover: Load balancers - Global Traffic Manager is a load balancer for Fans. It spreads traffic over eu-west stack and us-east stack, weighted.
Page Regions & Failover: Caches, limiters and schedulers - Nightly Snapshots is a scheduler (0 3 * * *) that starts Backup Job.
Page Start Here: A 5-Minute Tour holds nothing yet.
Scenarios - On-Sale Rush (Waiting Room), 6 steps: 10:00:00; EDGE; NO TOKEN; ADMITTED; SEAT MAP; MISS. - Buy Two Tickets (Hold → Pay → Confirm), 15 steps: 10:04 · BUY; TOKEN OK; SKIP THE LINE; GATEWAY; SIGNED IN · HUMAN; SEAT MAP; LOAD SECTION; HOLD 2 SEATS; LOCKED · 8 MIN; GREY ON EVERY MAP; CHECKOUT; AUTHORISED $184; SOLD; ORDER + OUTBOX; CONFIRMED. - Tickets Delivered (Async), 9 steps: CDC; LIVE SALES; ISSUE JOB; ONE ISSUER; PDF + PASS; ISSUED; IN YOUR WALLET; SMS (LEGACY); DOWNLOAD. - Card Processor A Outage, 5 steps: CHECKOUT; AUTHORISE; TIMEOUT · BREAKER OPENS; PROCESSOR B; SOLD ANYWAY. - Hold Expires: Seats Back On Sale, 3 steps: EVERY 30 S; RELEASE 312 HOLDS; BACK ON THE MAP. - Ticket Database Fails, 4 steps: HOLD; NO PRIMARY; MAP STILL SHOWS; TICKETS STALL.
Colours - Blue means Fan requests: what the fan is waiting on. - Green means Seats & orders: state that must be right. - Violet means Trust & money: identity, fraud, payments. - Amber means Async & live: events, queues, sockets. - Red means Fallbacks: failure paths and legacy.

g.text: • Never oversell: A seat is locked before it is shown as yours.
• Fair line: First in the room, first admitted.
• Six per fan: Enforced by Identity, per account.
• Known risk: Ticket DB has no standby yet.
HTTP · Token valid: skip the line
Turns a hold into an order
Fan requests — what the fan is waiting on
Seats & orders — state that must be right
